narrativeBlocks.title: The pantheon's clerk
narrativeBlocks.body: Thoth — ibis-headed — is the gods' scribe and record-keeper: he invented writing, keeps the divine accounts, and records the verdict at the Judgment of the Dead. Every Egyptian scribe worked under his patronage.

narrativeBlocks.title: Magic and words
narrativeBlocks.body: He is also lord of magic and sacred speech — the power of saying things truly. In Egypt's thought, writing is not mere record: the written word has power, and Thoth is its keeper.

narrativeBlocks.title: Five stolen days
narrativeBlocks.body: In one famous story, Thoth gambles with the moon-god and wins enough light to make five extra days — days outside the calendar where Nut can bear her children (Osiris, Isis, Set, and the rest). The calendar literally exists because he won a bet.

narrativeBlocks.title: The mediator
narrativeBlocks.body: When Horus and Set fight their succession-war, Thoth is the gods' mediator — the one who can be trusted by both sides. Scribes and wisdom-keepers keep order without swords.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why Thoth matters to you
narrativeBlocks.body: If you're reading written mythology at all, you're in Thoth's world — the Greeks borrowed him as Hermes Trismegistus and blamed the entire art of letters on him. The tradition you're studying IS his office.
